name: code-rubric-tight
description: Strict, checklist-style code-diagnosis rubric emphasizing objective grounding.

criteria.evaluation_criteria: Score must align with objective test outcomes and compile/runtime evidence.
quality_checks: Never assign high score when many tests fail.
Always cite concrete evidence for success/failure.

criteria.description: Reliability on boundaries and uncommon inputs.
criteria.evaluation_criteria: Edge handling must be evidenced by tests or explicit defensive logic.
binary_points: No crashes on malformed but in-scope inputs.
quality_checks: Penalize absent guards when edge requirements are explicit.
Do not infer edge robustness without evidence.

criteria.description: Suitability and efficiency of chosen approach.
criteria.evaluation_criteria: Use complexity and structural evidence to judge algorithm fit.
binary_points: Approach is logically valid for the problem class.
Complexity is reasonable for expected input scale.
quality_checks: Differentiate correctness bugs from inefficiency concerns.
Use specific code/test evidence for complexity claims.

criteria.evaluation_criteria: Readability, structure, and interface behavior should be judged from observable code.
binary_points: Avoids unexpected side effects (e.g., mutating input).
quality_checks: Prioritize contract violations over style preferences.

mistake_patterns: Hallucinated evidence or nonexistent test references.
Score inflation inconsistent with measured failures.
Non-actionable rationale not tied to objective signals.
